title: First Captive Breeding Report of Critically Endangered Wild Betta hendra
content:
ABSTRACT

The critically endangered Betta hendra, endemic to Borneo's peat swamp forests, faces severe threats from habitat loss and overharvesting. This study marks the first successful captive breeding of B. hendra, offering key insights for conservation. Males exhibited significantly higher growth rates (0.56 ± 0.07 mg/day) than females (p < 0.001). Male parental care ensured a 100% hatching rate but reduced larval growth due to food competition. Larvae reared without males but fed Artemia achieved the highest growth (6.22 ± 0.09 mm at 18 dph). These findings provide a framework for ex situ conservation, captive breeding, and sustainable management of B. hendra.
